groups.label: Product experience
groups.description: User-facing entry points and local review experiences.

children.label: User and command interfaces
children.description: Thin CLI, TUI and Simple-mode entry points. These should orchestrate application services rather than own audio, MIDI or persistence algorithms.

children.label: Workbench and review state
children.description: Local review projection, explicit decisions, transports, artifacts and GarageBand handoff. Playback and scores must remain separate from musical authority.

groups.label: Music processing
groups.description: Source preparation, separation, transcription, vocal work, instruments and rendering.

children.label: Stem separation
children.description: Public profiles and private evidence lanes. Open the focused subareas before individual modules.

children.label: Review and listening
children.description: Review pages, transports, approval records and human-listening projections. Playback remains non-authoritative.

children.label: Contracts and planning
children.description: Plans, requests, profiles, contracts and readiness decisions that constrain later execution.

children.label: Execution and supervision
children.description: Workers, runners, canaries, recovery, native execution and bounded inference machinery.

children.label: Evidence and evaluation
children.description: Outcome, report, metric, coverage, audit and parity evidence without activation authority.

children.label: Resources and adapters
children.description: Checkpoint, resource, runtime, adapter, artifact, process, sandbox, staging, lease and guard mechanics.

children.label: Source access and metadata
children.description: Local source validation, imports, immutable receipts, project manifests, roles, audio formats and musical metadata.

children.label: Vocals and comping
children.description: Vocal extraction, lyric- and phrase-bound analysis, draft review, comp evidence and bounded corrections. Human listening remains authoritative.

children.label: MIDI and transcription
children.description: Transcription, editable note data, timing transforms, alignment, role splitting, reusable clips and deterministic MIDI comparison.

children.label: Instruments and rendering
children.description: Starter sounds, instrument matching and preferences, SoundFont construction, playback, previews, timbre and MIDI-derived audio rendering.

groups.label: Research
groups.description: Optional comparison and research lanes that remain isolated from automatic product authority.

children.label: AI comparison and research
children.description: Isolated optional AI candidates, caches, workers, benchmarks and comparison evidence. Model execution is not implied by viewing this graph.

groups.label: Shared platform
groups.description: Cross-cutting product contracts, diagnostics, policies and modules not yet assigned to a more cohesive boundary.

children.label: Shared and product contracts
children.description: Cross-cutting data models, diagnostics, policies, product contracts and modules not yet assigned to a more cohesive architectural area.

contracts.description: Non-interface areas must not depend on the CLI or TUI entry modules.
The shared review transport must not depend on selection, MIDI, model or separation execution policy.
Source access and metadata modules should remain free of reciprocal static imports.
